iris.nec.failure.title: [%s] Not Enough Crashes detected!
iris.nec.failure.description:
Not Enough Crashes can severely break the game while handling crashes, and does not provide accurate results.
A good alternative is MixinTrace, which can identify the cause of a crash more reliably and does not put the game in an invalid state.

options.iris.shadowDistance.enabled: Allows you to change the maximum distance for shadows. Terrain and entities beyond this distance will not cast shadows. Lowering the shadow distance can significantly increase performance.
options.iris.shadowDistance.disabled: Your current shader pack has already set a render distance for shadows; you cannot change it.
options.iris.shadowDistance.sodium_toolt: The shadow render distance controls how far away terrain can potentially be rendered in the shadow pass. Lower distances mean that less terrain will be rendered, improving frame rates. This option cannot be changed on packs which explicitly specify a shadow render distance. The actual shadow render distance is capped by the View Distance setting.
options.pauc.vanillaFog.tooltip: Toggles the vanilla distance fog dome. Underwater and lava fog are not affected. Disabling it also removes the LOD horizon fade that rides on the same fog.
options.pauc.lodDistance.tooltip: Sets how many PauC LOD rings are added beyond the vanilla view distance. Vanilla chunks render first, then PauC extends the horizon by this extra amount.
options.pauc.shadows.tooltip: PauC terrain shadows without any shader pack: the sun casts real shadows from hills, cliffs, trees and builds. Higher settings give crisper, longer shadows.
options.pauc.nvidiaAcceleration.tooltip: Allows PauC to use optional NVIDIA/CUDA worker paths when the GPU and driver are detected. CPU fallback remains active.
options.pauc.terrainMorphing.tooltip: Smooths the vanilla-to-LOD terrain boundary without shaders. Players can disable it if the local transition jitters.
options.pauc.dynamicResolution.tooltip: Adjusts internal shader resolution in guarded steps to support FPS. Disabled by default.
options.iris.colorSpace.sodium_tooltip: The color space to transform the screen to. Works on top of shader packs. Use SRGB if unsure.
